articles.title: China’s Huawei Convicted in U.S. Over Bank Fraud, Iran Ties
articles.summary: China’s biggest technology firm and the world’s largest telecommunications equipment maker has been convicted in the U.S. of stealing trade secrets and defrauding banks about its business in Iran. Huawei was found guilty on 10 of 12 counts by a jury in Brooklyn on Tuesday. The verdict all but brings to a close an almost eight-year-long criminal case against Huawei and three of its subsidiaries. articles.title: How AI Is Changing What Companies Know About Their Customers
articles.summary: Fifteen years ago, when he worked as an adviser to the pharmaceutical industry, Jeff Gaus’ firm bought drugstore cash-register data. From those records, he says, the company could tell pharma reps that, for example, “Dr. Smith has three people with this condition” and instruct them to go pitch their wares to that doctor. articles.title: Trump Gives ‘America’s Mayor’ the Presidential Medal of Freedom
articles.summary: President Donald Trump on Tuesday presented Rudy Giuliani, the former Mayor of New York City who served as Trump’s personal lawyer in 2020, with the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Appearing on Steve Bannon’s War Room podcast on Monday, Giuliani said that he was “very, very humbled and very honored” by the recognition. Giuliani rose to prominence as a prosecutor in New York and was first elected Mayor of New York City in 1993 as a Republican.
